claims.claim: **Do a comprehensive assessment when a new patient scores pain 2 or more** on a zero-to-10 numerical rating scale, **or an existing patient reports a new pain or a sudden, unexpected change in intensity.**
claims.source_text: a new patient reports a pain score of 2 or more on self-reported numerical rating scale of zero to 10 … an existing patient reports a new pain or a sudden, unexpected change in intensity of pain

claims.claim: **If cognitive impairment makes self-report difficult, use the Abbey Pain Scale.**
claims.source_text: If self-reporting of pain intensity is difficult due to cognitive impairment, use the Abbey Pain Scale

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider an oncological emergency** as the cause: fracture (or imminent fracture), brain, epidural or leptomeningeal metastasis, infection, or an obstructed or perforated abdominal organ.
claims.source_text: Consider whether the pain is related to an oncological emergency, e.g: bone fracture (or high risk of imminent fracture) brain metastasis epidural metastasis leptomeningeal metastasis infection obstructed or perforated abdominal organ
claims.locator: Cancer Council Australia, 'Cancer pain management in adults', v2.4, published 2026-05-13, MAGICapp https://app.magicapp.org/#/guideline/jXXAdj, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tell every patient starting opioids that constipation is very common**, and teach preventive bowel care.
